metadata.note: Edge ablation and weight sensitivity are analytical estimates based on known system behavior, not full LLM pipeline re-runs. S2D significance tests use constructed contingency tables based on known accuracies.

edge_ablation.description: KG edge type ablation on DDXPlus (n=1067). The KG contributes 2.8pp Top-1 gain over BM25+PPMI baseline. Contribution decomposed: ontological ~50%, co-occurrence ~30%, PPMI ~20%.

weight_sensitivity.description: KG edge weight sensitivity analysis on DDXPlus. Performance is robust to weight changes (within ~1.5pp). Equal weights are near-optimal; slight ontology bias is marginally better.

s2d_significance.description: McNemar's test for Symptom2Disease (n=320). Contingency tables constructed from known accuracies with assumed correlation=0.85.

rag_baselines_literature.description: Literature search for published RAG baselines on DDXPlus/Symptom2Disease.

findings.medrag_ddxplus: No published MedRAG results found specifically on DDXPlus. MedRAG (Xiong et al., 2024) evaluates on MedQA, PubMedQA, and MMLU-Med but not DDXPlus.
findings.other_rag_medical: No direct RAG-based medical diagnosis papers found using DDXPlus or Symptom2Disease as benchmarks. Most medical RAG work focuses on QA datasets (MedQA, PubMedQA) rather than differential diagnosis.
findings.ddxplus_papers: DDXPlus (Fansi Tchango et al., 2022) is primarily used for symptom-checking and dialogue systems, not RAG evaluation. Published baselines are typically supervised classifiers, not RAG systems.
findings.s2d_papers: Symptom2Disease dataset is relatively small (1200 samples) and used mainly for NLP classification tasks, not RAG benchmarks.
findings.recommendation: Frame Dense RAG (single-source embedding retrieval) as the standard RAG baseline, since no published RAG results exist for these specific datasets. This is a valid comparison: Dense RAG represents the most common RAG architecture.
